headline: OpenAI reports an automated Linux pipeline that reproduced 1,724 kernel vulnerabilities and generated 948 distinct local privilege-escalation patches
summary: OpenAI describes a controlled prototype that scanned selected Linux kernel audit targets using an upcoming cyber model and agent pipeline. In a run it says occurred in mid-October 2026, the system produced 2,308 candidate findings, dynamically reproduced 1,724, generated 291 information-leak proofs of concept and 1,169 working local privilege-escalation exploits, then developed 948 distinct patches after variant analysis. OpenAI reports API-credit cost of about USD 1.21 million. These are first-party results from one specified workflow: independent reproduction, maintainer acceptance of the patches, transfer to other systems, and generalized security impact are not established.
